items.title: Amazon RDS for MySQL supports MySQL minor version 8.4.13
items.content_snippet: Starting today, Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for MySQL supports MySQL minor version 8.4.13, the latest minor released by community MySQL. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and new functionality added by the MySQL community. items.title: Amazon Cognito now supports point-in-time recovery
items.content_snippet: Amazon Cognito now supports point-in-time recovery (PITR), so you can restore the user data in a user pool to an earlier time. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices. Previously, you had to build and maintain your own export and restore process, and restored users received new identifiers and had to reset their passwords. items.title: Amazon RDS now supports fast storage volume initialization
items.content_snippet: Amazon RDS now initializes storage volumes faster when you perform a point-in-time restore (PITR), create a read replica, or convert a Single-AZ instance to Multi-AZ. Each of these operations creates storage volumes from a snapshot, and the data blocks are downloaded from Amazon S3 before you can access them. items.title: AWS Control Tower now supports existing Amazon S3 bucket for log delivery
items.content_snippet: AWS Control Tower now lets you use an existing Amazon S3 bucket in your landing zone to store AWS Config and AWS CloudTrail logs. Previously, AWS Control Tower required you to use the Amazon S3 bucket it creates and manages for log storage. Now, customers who want full control of bucket policies, lifecycle rules, and logging infrastructure can consolidate centralized logs in an Amazon S3 bucket they already manage. items.title: 2026 in LLMs — Simon Willison
items.content_snippet: Simon Willison used AI coding agents to locate a beeping detector buried in 40 boxes. At CODE Summit 2026, the Datasette creator traces three LLM inflection points: reliable coding agents, persistent problem solving and vibe coded game development. Pelican benchmarks, prompt injection and rogue agents frame a broader question about developer productivity: why does software engineering still feel harder?
